I.prompt: Image 1 is my ORIGINAL M, the only style reference. Draw exactly ONE new capital I as a sibling in this heavy organic ribbon font. IMPORTANT: this is a SANS-SERIF I made from ONE BROAD RISING STEM, NOT the conventional serif I. There are NO separate horizontal bars across the top or bottom. Imagine the M's heavy left rising leg as a complete independent letter: a gently forward-leaning thick white ribbon, softly convex sides, a rounded crest, slight natural taper and a compact rounded-flat foot. Keep the silhouette subtly asymmetric and the stroke just as bold as M at the same visible cap height. A very small natural flare at each end is allowed, but no projecting slab serifs, crossbar, long L arm, J hook, detached dot, thin slash or swash. This must read cleanly as uppercase I inside TIME and INITIAL when the letters are widely spaced. The letter is tall and optically compact, roughly half as wide as its height including its lean. It should belong to M's soft flowing family, not a generic geometric rectangle or an italic Times Roman I. Render ONLY the one solid white filled letter on pure black, centered with generous margins. No M, other letters, words, outlines, borders, shadows, texture, guides or labels.

rejectedAttempts.prompt: Generate exactly ONE uppercase I for this custom ribbon typeface. Image 1 is our original M and the ONLY positive style master. Image 2 is the old I to improve, NOT a style to copy. Image 3 shows the user's widely spaced TIME: the old I's rigid matching horizontal caps look like a borrowed italic serif font beside the flowing T, M and E. Draw a better I with the same broad, heavy, gently forward-rising ribbon as M's main ascending stroke. Use subtle asymmetric curvature and compact softly flared terminals that grow naturally from the stem: a soft upper shoulder and a restrained rounded-flat lower finish. The ends must not be two long parallel horizontal slab serifs. Keep enough understated top/bottom definition to read clearly as uppercase I, without becoming T, L, J or a thin slash. Keep the stem substantial and the total width optically compact, approximately two-thirds of its cap height, with M's quiet rounded joins and strong black-and-white silhouette. No decorative hooks or flourishes. The I must feel drawn by the same designer as M when widely spaced in TIME, not merely rounded from a conventional serif I. Output ONLY the one finished white filled I on a pure black square, upright at the original M's cap-height placement with generous black margins. No other letters, words, labels, comparison panels, outlines, shadows, texture or guides. Do not redraw or change M, T, E or S.
